body:
Three institutional investors have committed a combined $345 million to Accel-KKR Strategic Capital II, with one putting the fund's size at $2.5 billion.

The vehicle targets single-asset continuation deals involving private equity-backed companies in the middle and lower-middle markets.

The single-asset continuation vehicle strategy has deployed about 40% of its capital and has a $5 billion hard cap.

"We're turning down most of the deals we see to focus purely on exactly those very few deals that the GPs really want to hold onto," said CEO Benoît Durteste.

The planned offering will sit within KKR Solutions, a platform spanning sports investments and GP financing that CFO Rob Lewin expects to grow to more than $100 billion in AUM over time.

The firm held the final close of its debut infrastructure secondaries fund during the quarter, reaching its $1.5 billion hard cap and marking StepStone's largest inaugural fundraise to date.

The strategy, anchored by a Korean institutional investor, has adopted an evergreen semi-liquid structure aimed at capturing emerging credit secondary opportunities throughout the cycle.

TPG GP Solutions II, which held a first close last year, had raised over $1.7 billion in capital commitments as of June.

NorthSands Capital I targets single-asset continuation vehicles in well-known sectors, including industrials and industrial services companies.

The firm recently closed its debut GP-led fund, which focuses on single-asset CVs, with over $3.6 billion in capital commitments.
